# Setting up Claude Code {.unnumbered} Claude Code is an AI agentAn assistant that can read across a project’s files and, depending on its permission mode, edit them and run commands, such as Claude Code. An agent acts; a chat window only advises. that runs in the Terminal tab of RStudio or Positron. It reads, edits and runs the files in your project, asking your permission as it goes. You need very little terminal: one command to start it, and the R console and Git pane for everything else. *⏱ ~30 minutes, before the workshop day.* If a command here fails, check the [Claude Code setup page](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/setup) first. ## Before you install: three questions 1. **Are you permitted to use it on this work?** Claude Code sends what it reads, and the output of commands it runs, to Anthropic. Check your institution's policy and, near research data, your ethics approval and data agreements ([Block 4](11d-context-disclosure-autonomy.qmd)). 2. **Which account?** A Claude Pro or Max subscription, a Claude for Teams or Enterprise seat, a Claude Console account (billed per request), or access your institution has set up through a cloud provider. 3. **Is your computer supported?** macOS 13 or later, Windows 10 (1809) or later, or a recent Linux. ## Step 1: Open the Terminal tab in your IDE - **RStudio:** the **Terminal** tab next to the Console. - **Positron:** *Terminal → New Terminal*. With a project open, the Terminal tab starts in the project's root folder, which is where Claude Code needs to run. You never need to `cd`. **Which shell is it?** A prompt starting `PS` is **PowerShell** (Windows); one ending `$` is **Git Bash** (Windows) or bash/zsh (macOS, Linux). ## Step 2: Check git and R are reachable **In the terminal:** ```bash git --version Rscript --version ``` Both should print a version number. - **`git` not found:** install git (on Windows, **Git for Windows**). - **`Rscript` not found (common on Windows):** run `R.home("bin")` in the R console and add that folder to your `PATH` (Windows: Start menu → "Edit environment variables for your account" → **Path**). Then **quit and reopen RStudio or Positron**: its terminals keep the `PATH` they started with. ## Step 3: Install Claude Code **macOS or Linux,** in the terminal: ```bash curl -fsSL https://claude.ai/install.sh | bash ``` **Windows,** in PowerShell (a prompt starting `PS`; if your Terminal tab is Git Bash, open the **PowerShell** app for this one step): ```powershell irm https://claude.ai/install.ps1 | iex ``` Then **quit and reopen RStudio or Positron**, and check the version in the Terminal tab: ```bash claude --version ``` **You are done when** it prints **2.1.281 or later**, so that Claude Code reads your `AGENTS.md` instruction file directly. ## Before you sign in: prepare your workshop repository 1. **Fork, clone and open the template** in one step, in the R console: `usethis::create_from_github("/", fork = TRUE)`. Your instructor gives you the exact name. 2. **Restore the packages:** `renv::restore()` in the R console, once. It installs the versions in the template's lockfileThe renv.lock file that records the R version and the exact package versions a project uses, so renv::restore() can rebuild the same environment. and can take several minutes. 3. **Commit** in the Git pane (RStudio) or Source Control view (Positron), so the day starts clean. The course skillsA folder containing a SKILL.md file (and optionally scripts and templates) that an assistant loads only when it is invoked by name or judged relevant from its description. already ship in both `.agents/skills/` and `.claude/skills/`. :::{.callout-tip collapse="true"} ## Using Posit Assistant Posit Assistant needs no terminal install: it is built into RStudio and Positron and configured there. Check that your account or provider key works before the day; [Block 4](11d-context-disclosure-autonomy.qmd) lists the options. ::: ## Your workshop repository Every block from Block 4 works in this one repository. The template ships most of it; files marked *you* are created during the day. ``` data/ raw/voles_metabolism.csv Blocks 2–5, 9 and 10 (one deliberate NA) raw/voles_raw.csv Block 7 (errors planted by your instructor) derived/ written by Block 7's cleaning docs/ data_note.md the data provider's note (Block 7) codebook.csv you, Block 7 ai-log.md you, from Block 4 scripts/ explore_voles.R Block 4 (exploratory, so unnumbered) 00_profile.R … 03_audit_cleaning.R Block 7: the cleaning pipeline 04_load_data.R, 05_analysis.R Block 9: the analysis functions/ load_voles.R, validate_voles.R, and summary_functions.R (Block 9) tests/ make_reference.R, test_cleaning.R fixtures/ the raw-data checksum (shipped) and the reference you capture in Block 9 AGENTS.md the instruction file (you edit it in Block 5) .agents/skills/, .claude/skills/ skills (copies of the same folders) .claude/settings.json Manual mode and the deny rules (Block 6) renv.lock the package versions ``` `.claude/settings.json` holds the deny rulesA permission rule in the deny list of .claude/settings.json that stops Claude Code’s built-in tools from editing or reading the matching files. It checks shell output redirects such as > file, but not R code or most other commands that change the same files. that protect the raw data, the codebook, the checks and the references; you read and test it in [Block 6](11f-enforced-controls.qmd). Scripts are numbered in the order they run. ## Step 4: Sign in With your workshop project open, type `claude` in its Terminal tab. On first launch a browser window opens: sign in with your account (`/logout` and `/login` switch accounts later). If a Terminal tab was open before you switched projects, close it and open a new one. :::{.callout-warning collapse="true"} ## Using an API key If you use a Console API key, set it as `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`, for example in `.Renviron`, and never commit that file. The template denies Claude Code reading a `.Renviron` in the project folder, but not the one in your home folder. If `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` is already set for another tool, Claude Code may use it instead of your subscription and bill per request: check under `/config`. ::: ## Step 5: The essentials Your workshop repository starts Claude Code in **Manual** mode (`default`), a permission modeThe setting that decides how much Claude Code may do without asking: plan (read only), default (asks before edits and commands), acceptEdits (edits without asking) and bypassPermissions (never asks). in which it asks before every edit and command. Claude Code's own default is `auto`, where a second model approves actions for you; the project setting overrides it. Read each request before you approve it. Shift+Tab changes the mode, `/plan` asks for a plan first, and the [Claude Code quick reference](11-AI-programming-integrated.qmd#cc-quick-reference) lists the rest. ### Where am I typing? {#where-am-i-typing} | Where | What runs there | |---|---| | The Claude Code prompt, inside the Terminal tab | Your requests to Claude Code. A line starting `!` runs a shell command, and its output is added to the conversation, so it reaches the model too. | | The terminal's own prompt (`PS`, `$` or `%`), after `/exit` | Shell commands: `claude`, git, `Rscript` | | The R console | R code. Claude Code cannot see it, or anything you load there. | | The Git pane (RStudio) or Source Control view (Positron) | Git status, diffs, reverting and committing, on the same repository | While Claude Code is running, the Terminal tab belongs to it, so check its work somewhere else. ### Checking work while Claude Code is running {#checking-work} | To check... | In the R console or Git pane | |---|---| | What changed | The Git pane: **Diff** shows the changes line by line; **Revert** undoes one you did not want. | | That a script runs in a fresh R session | `callr::rscript(here::here("scripts", "name.R"))`, or *Session → Restart R* and then `source()` it | | That the tests pass in a fresh R session | `callr::r(\(d) testthat::test_dir(d), list(here::here("tests")))` | | That the packages match the lockfile | `renv::status()` | These work the same on Windows, macOS and Linux. Each `Rscript` call Claude Code makes is a fresh R process too, so objects never carry over to it from your console. :::{.callout-note collapse="true"} ## At the command line The same checks from a terminal (after `/exit`, or in a second Terminal tab): `git status`, `git diff`, `git restore `, `Rscript scripts/name.R`, `Rscript -e "testthat::test_dir('tests')"` and `Rscript -e "renv::status()"`. ::: ## Step 6: Check everything works :::{.task} ::::{.task-header} Pre-workshop check (15 minutes) :::: ::::{.task-container} **Start state:** your workshop project is open, and the Git pane shows no uncommitted changes. **1. Manual mode, and a plan.** Type `claude` in the Terminal tab. It should say it is in Manual mode (`default`), not `auto`. Then: ```text /plan Describe the structure of this repository and what each top-level folder contains. Do not change anything. ``` **2. R is reachable.** ```text Run Rscript -e "sessionInfo()" and show me the output. ``` Approve the command when asked: you should see your R version. **3. Settings and instructions load.** `/permissions` should list the deny rules, and `/memory` should list `AGENTS.md`. On a Pro or Max account, also open `/privacy-settings` and decide whether your conversations may be used for model training. Type `/exit`. **4. The project is ready.** In the R console: ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ```{.r .cell-code} renv::status() callr::r(\(d) testthat::test_dir(d), list(here::here("tests"))) ``` ::: `renv::status()` should report no problems, and the tests should run with **no failures**: most skip for now, waiting for the block that creates their files. **5. Inline completion works.** In a new R script, type `# Calculate the mean of 1 to 100`: grey suggested text should appear ([Block 2](11b-inline-completions.qmd) uses it first). **6. The checkpoint branches are there.** The Git pane's branch menu should show `block5-done`, `block7-done` and `block9-done`. Stay on `main`. **You are done when** the Git pane shows no changes, Claude Code starts in Manual mode, `/permissions` lists the deny rules, and the tests run with no failures. Copy the output of steps 2–4 into a text file to bring on the day. **If it goes wrong:** `Rscript` not found, return to Step 2; empty `/permissions` list, start `claude` from the workshop project's Terminal tab; a changed file, **Revert** in the Git pane; package problems, run `renv::restore()` again and send the error to your instructor before the day. :::: ::: ## Going further (not covered live) This material is not covered in the live session. Work through it afterwards if it is useful to you. ### Other install routes and shells - **macOS with Homebrew:** `brew install --cask claude-code` (update it by hand; the native installer updates itself). - **Changing the Terminal tab's shell:** in RStudio, *Tools → Global Options → Terminal → New terminals open with*; in Positron, the drop-down beside **+** in the terminal panel. - **Windows:** Claude Code runs its own commands in Git Bash if Git for Windows is installed, and in PowerShell if not; either works for this course. - **Skills missing?** If `.claude/skills/clean-with-codebook/SKILL.md` does not exist, copy the folders in the R console: `fs::dir_copy(here::here(".agents", "skills"), here::here(".claude", "skills"), overwrite = TRUE)`. On macOS or Linux a symbolic linkA file-system entry that points to another folder or file, so one copy can appear in two places. On Windows, copying the folder is usually simpler. also works ([Block 5](11e-instructions-skills.qmd)). ### Where Claude Code fits among the course's tools | | Claude Code | Posit Assistant | GitHub Copilot | |---|---|---|---| | Where it runs | The Terminal tab of RStudio or Positron | Inside RStudio or Positron | Your editor, github.com, and GitHub's servers (cloud agent) | | What it sees | Project files, and output of commands it runs | Your live R session and project files | Open files; on github.com, the repository | | Instruction file | `AGENTS.md` (read directly) | `AGENTS.md` | `AGENTS.md`, `.github/copilot-instructions.md` | | Skills folder | `.claude/skills/` | `.agents/skills/` | `.agents/skills/`, `.claude/skills/`, `.github/skills/` | ## Glossary ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ::: {.cell-output-display} `````{=html}
term definition
agent An assistant that can read across a project's files and, depending on its permission mode, edit them and run commands, such as Claude Code. An agent acts; a chat window only advises.
deny rule A permission rule in the deny list of .claude/settings.json that stops Claude Code's built-in tools from editing or reading the matching files. It checks shell output redirects such as > file, but not R code or most other commands that change the same files.
lockfile The renv.lock file that records the R version and the exact package versions a project uses, so renv::restore() can rebuild the same environment.
permission mode The setting that decides how much Claude Code may do without asking: plan (read only), default (asks before edits and commands), acceptEdits (edits without asking) and bypassPermissions (never asks).
skill A folder containing a SKILL.md file (and optionally scripts and templates) that an assistant loads only when it is invoked by name or judged relevant from its description.
symbolic link A file-system entry that points to another folder or file, so one copy can appear in two places. On Windows, copying the folder is usually simpler.
````` ::: ::: ## References - Claude Code documentation: *Advanced setup*, ; *Authentication*, ; *Permission modes*, .
